title: How Firm AI is changing the way investment banks find and win mandates
summary: Read this Q&A with Intapp’s Brian Bissonette to learn how Firm AI provides a lasting competitive advantage by helping bankers find and close business faster.
body_markdown:
**What can Firm AI help investment banks do that wasn’t previously possible?**


BRIAN BISSONETTE


Turn proprietary data into a competitive advantage.


Proprietary data includes the enormous amount of client information living within emails, meeting notes, committee memos, and various other places. It’s valuable not only to the banker who initially captured it, but also oftentimes to the rest of the organization. An insight from one client conversation could inform next week’s pitch or help the bank win an opportunity years down the road.


But this data isn’t very useful when it’s buried in multiple locations. Banks need a way to capture it in the right system of record. They also need to make it accessible, either directly or indirectly, to one or more large-language models (LLMs), where it can be used to generate reliable and contextualized outputs.


Firm AI addresses both needs. It uses zero data entry to passively capture proprietary data from emails, meeting notes, documents, and other sources, then log it in a system of record. It also makes this data available to one or more LLMs and additional firm systems, where it’s leveraged alongside public data to execute a range of tasks that include creating buyer or investor recommendations, surfacing real-time client insights, and drafting outreach emails.


As proprietary intelligence is captured, it becomes part of Firm AI’s context engine. In Intapp’s case, this context engine is purpose-built for investment banking. The result is a self-replenishing body of invaluable institutional knowledge that allows the AI to deliver increasingly relevant insights and recommendations — so banks can make better-informed decisions, move faster, and ultimately win more mandates.


The importance of the context engine is difficult to overstate. It’s what allows agentic AI coworkers to operate with an understanding of the unique taxonomy and argot of M&A and capital markets.


**Where do you see AI having the biggest impact within the deal lifecycle?**


BRIAN BISSONETTE


AI will definitely help banks address the many challenges associated with deal execution, but I think it will have the biggest impact in the earlier stages of the deal lifecycle, particularly origination.


Origination is intensely competitive, and identifying which companies are likely to sell, acquire, or access the capital markets is difficult — much more art than science.


Bankers can’t effectively cover every company, venture fund, and private equity firm in their sector or vertical because, in most cases, there are simply too many. They need to narrow their focus to organizations that fit their coverage criteria, and that are likely to transact.


The latter requires building relationships with the people who influence whether a company pursues a transaction, and which bank is chosen to advise on or underwrite it. Relationship-building takes years, and the process has become more complex as the number of parties involved in banker selection has expanded beyond the company itself to include influential investors and other stakeholders.


Right now, no person or technology can identify which companies are ready to acquire, sell, or raise capital with 100% accuracy. While some signals are relatively clear, such as approaching debt maturities or publicly stated plans to, for example, go public, others are much harder to anticipate and depend on hundreds or even thousands of company-specific, investor-specific, and macroeconomic considerations.


[Firm AI](https://www.intapp.com/downloadable/firm-ai/) , however, can help bankers focus on clients likely to transact, and uncover more promising prospects by analyzing proprietary firm intelligence alongside public market data including company size, financials like revenue, revenue growth, profitability, available or required capital, stated plans, and strategic imperatives. It quickly surfaces companies that meet the firm’s criteria and capabilities, so bankers can spend their time where it’s likely to produce the highest return.


Firm AI can also help bankers understand which relationships will give them an advantage in winning mandates. By bringing together institutional knowledge and relationship intelligence scattered across individual bankers, teams, and systems, it can generate relationship maps that reveal who knows whom and how those connections extend to key decision-makers. This exposes connections that might not have surfaced otherwise. For example, it might show that a colleague on another team knows a board member or influential investor at a prospective client.


Together, these capabilities give banks a competitive advantage by providing a clear picture of where the best opportunities lie and how to pursue them.


> Firm AI can help bankers focus on clients likely to transact, and uncover more promising prospects by analyzing proprietary firm intelligence alongside public market data.
>
>
> **Brian Bissonette** , Industry Principal, Investment Banking, Intapp


**How can AI help bankers reduce the manual work involved in winning new business?**


BRIAN BISSONETTE


One area where AI can help is[pitch preparation](https://www.intapp.com/celeste/use-cases/build-a-client-ready-proposal/) — it’s a major bottleneck.


Any senior banker will tell you that if they could, they would be out pitching more ideas to more clients. But creating a thoughtful, bespoke pitch is very involved and extremely time-consuming — in most cases even a conventional pitch consumes an enormous amount of energy and human capital. Every slide has to be just right, because it’s really, really hard for banks to get hired, even when they’re invited to bake-off for a planned deal.


AI can take a lot of the tedious work out of pitch creation so that bankers can analyze and present ideas much faster than they do now. With[Firm AI](https://www.intapp.com/celeste) , bankers can almost instantly produce client-ready materials that showcase their firm’s most relevant experience and proven successes, generate accurate financial models, and draft compelling slides — all without digging through old decks, combing through SEC filings, or manually entering data. The AI even figures out who’s free to staff the pitch.


And the work’s not done when the deck is done. Properly preparing for a pitch or any other type of client meeting for that matter is also a traditionally painful but critically important activity. No banker wants to give an actual or prospective client the impression that they’re just one of dozens or hundreds of people the banker needs to pay attention to. Proper preparation can mean hours and hours of work sifting through multiple data sources, having live conversations, and documenting important details.


Firm AI makes[meeting prep](https://www.intapp.com/celeste/use-cases/create-a-pre-meeting-brief/) easy with a playbook that does all the heavy lifting. With the click of a button, it summarizes prior client conversations and relevant public information, including news, financial metrics, and management or board changes. This way, the banker arrives prepared, informed, and ready to have a meaningful conversation — and the client can see that the banker has been paying attention and has thought carefully about their business.


**What does AI mean for industry compliance and regulatory expectations?**


BRIAN BISSONETTE


In investment banking, the regulatory standard often rises to the technology that’s broadly available. So as it becomes increasingly possible for your average investment bank to complete work with AI and use that AI to produce audit reports showing, for example, who has seen what data and when, regulators will eventually expect every bank to do the same.


We’re already seeing early indications that regulators are expecting a deep level of compliance that may not be expressly stated as requiring AI, but that realistically will be difficult to achieve reliably without it.


Banks should be taking steps now to implement AI that will allow them to meet these evolving standards so they aren’t caught unprepared. They need to prioritize compliance from the outset, rather than adopting AI and discovering later that it can’t meet their requirements. And AI that’s “close enough” or “pretty good” at compliance won’t suffice.


Firm AI is uniquely suited to meeting industry compliance requirements, and, when necessary, demonstrating compliance because it’s built to understand and enforce an investment bank’s policies and rules, and apply them consistently. And since it works much more quickly than a human, it can surface risks that otherwise might not have been spotted.


> Firm AI is uniquely suited to meeting industry compliance requirements, and, when necessary, demonstrating compliance because it’s built to understand and enforce an investment bank’s policies and rules, and apply them consistently.
>
>
> **Brian Bissonette** , Industry Principal, Investment Banking, Intapp


**How can Firm AI accelerate career development for junior bankers?**


BRIAN BISSONETTE


Firm AI can help junior bankers spend less time on routine, process-oriented tasks like data collection and more time on financial and strategic analysis — the work they were trained to do and want to do.


Firm AI can also help junior bankers become better coverage officers earlier in their careers. Because they don’t own client relationships or wallet-share targets, their view of the business is usually limited to the work immediately in front of them. Firm AI changes that by giving them access to firmwide data. They can query data using natural language and get answers almost instantly. They can request insight into the dynamics behind different pitches, why the bank is pursuing a particular opportunity, how it’s positioning itself, which pitches have won or lost, and just about anything else.


This broad perspective helps junior bankers understand how the bank develops business, what clients are looking for, and what it takes to win a mandate. Over time, they can apply those insights to their own client interactions and develop the judgment they need to provide strong coverage.
